title: Sokat, Eleget – How Much You Do Something

sections.title: Quantity adverbs next to the verb
sections.content: sokat ("a lot") and eleget ("enough") sit right next to the verb to describe how much you do something — Sokat mozgok ("I exercise a lot"), Eleget alszom ("I sleep enough"). Both are built from adjectives you already know, sok and elég, with the same -t ending you've seen mark a quantity or an object.

items.english: I exercise a lot every day.
He/she doesn't move much, so he/she is tired.

sections.content: keveset ("a little, not much") is the natural opposite of sokat, built the same way from kevés — useful the moment you want to describe a habit that falls short.
